_comment: CAMPAIGN 04 -- NEEDS AN ELEVATED WINDOW. Do not run this from an ordinary
shell; tools/ttd_record.ps1 refuses to run non-elevated and will fail the
probe closed, which is correct behaviour and not a bug to work around.
WHY THIS EXISTS. Campaign 03 found that `BuildLandscapeCache` issued from
autoexec.con access-violates 3 times out of 3 at level 100 -- 0xC0000005,
an OnslaughtException.txt created at 0 bytes, and the MemStats on the next
line never running, so the fault is inside the command. `BuildStaticShadows`
in the identical position is clean 3/3.
A deterministic crash is the cheapest TTD target there is. One trace of it
yields the exact fault address, the call path into the landscape bake, and
the engine's own exception path. All three are dark across every one of the
69 coverage indexes, and the bake pipeline is game code -- below the
0x00570000 D3DX9 boundary -- so every byte it lights is Aquila's own.
THE SHADOWS ARM IS THE CONTROL, and it is not optional. It runs the same
level, the same launch and the same recorder, differing by one command that
does not crash. Without it, everything the landscape trace lights is
confounded with level load: a level-100 trace lights level-100 code whether
or not the command did anything, and the delta against a matched clean take
is the only thing that isolates the bake path.
SIZING IS UNCERTAIN AND I COULD NOT MEASURE IT. TTD slows this game about
62x (301 recorded seconds = 4.85 s of game time, measured 2026-08-01). The
crash lands ~11 s of game time after launch, most of which is level load, so
a naive extrapolation says ~11 minutes of wall clock and something like
20-30 GiB against a 32 GiB cap. That extrapolation assumes level load costs
the recorder what gameplay costs it, which is probably wrong in an unknown
direction -- load is I/O-bound and gameplay is CPU-bound. recordSeconds is
set to 900 so the recorder is not the thing that ends the run; ttd_record.ps1
owns the size cap and the drive policy and will stop it if it must.
IF IT IS TOO BIG: drop recordSeconds, or run the shadows control first --
it is the same length and does not crash, so it sizes the landscape arm for
free and costs one take.
PREDICTION, REGISTERED IN ADVANCE. This commit precedes the first run.
T1  The landscape trace ends in a fault and the coverage delta against the
shadows control lights bodies in the landscape/poly-bucket bake below
FALSIFIED BY: a delta whose newly-lit bodies are all above 0x00570000
(that would put the crash inside D3DX9, not Aquila, and would also fire
the RE-PROBE-CATALOGUE section 1.3 falsifier), or a delta of zero new
bodies (the crash is in code already covered, and the interesting part
is a branch rather than a body).
Check it with:
py -3 tools/re_coverage_ledger.py delta --before <base> --after <new>
SCOPE. Level 100, this machine, this GPU, this driver. A bake path is
exactly the kind of code that is hardware-conditional, so a crash here is
not yet a claim that the shipped game crashes for anyone else.

probes.name: ttd-landscape-crash-r1
probes.note: The crash under TTD. Expect the recorder to survive the target faulting; ttd_record.ps1 owns that, not this manifest.

probes.name: ttd-shadows-control-r1
probes.note: THE MATCHED CONTROL. Same level, same launch, same recorder, one command different and it does not crash. The landscape trace means nothing without this to subtract.
